Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

Allica Bank aims to provide Expert Banking for Business Britain by providing excellent customer experience and pioneering technology solutions to facilitate this.

The Autonomous Lending tribe runs across multiple business lines including Credit Operations and Underwriting, with a mission to build AI-first lending origination journeys, automating origination capabilities, data flows, and underwriting and operational workflow management.

The tribe is a critical driver for Allica to continue to realise its vision of providing a market leading relationship-based banking experience, at a speed and cost to serve the rest of the market cannot match.

Role Description
The Product Owner will lead the work to define, deliver and manage AI-enabled products across our lending journeys, bringing together product design and thinking with a strong working knowledge of what today’s AI can and cannot do.

You will be accountable for the roadmap of your team and for the full product lifecycle: discovery and design, day-to-day delivery, launch and adoption by colleagues and customers, and how risks are addressed once a product is live. You will aim to build robust, automated and well-governed systems and processes that enable us to move quickly and innovate our lending and financing products in the SME banking market.

Whilst a lot of the market aims to avoid the complex nature of SME businesses, we are going for it head on, designing simple and efficient solutions to the most complex problems in the market to provide excellent and efficient customer experience. We aim for our external view of the lending product, as well as our internal systems to be the best in market which will allow us to scale quickly to serve more UK SMEs, while doing so in a cost-effective manner.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Responsible for innovation and building end-to-end solutions for AI-enabled lending product, origination, underwriting and operational flows

  • Lead a small cross-functional team (e.g. a full stack engineer and AI specialist) to deliver your roadmap

  • Continuously review business needs, refine priorities and iterate towards measurable outcomes – judged on fewer requests for further information, more applications decided with AI, less colleague time per application across underwriting and credit operations, and risk outcomes no worse than the equivalent manual journey

  • Prototype and experiment quickly – vibe-code working prototypes yourself, close enough to the real thing that an engineer can harden it into production code

  • Determine the accuracy of AI solutions by analysing the data yourself and building the verified “ground truth” datasets that results are tested against, working with underwriters and credit operations colleagues to agree what a correct answer looks like

  • Take responsibility for launch and adoption – briefing stakeholders, training the teams who will use the product, and closing the loop on the feedback they give back

  • Produce the written work that keeps delivery moving and safe – clear descriptions of what we are building and why, a record of the important design decisions and trade-offs made, and the assessments needed to get a product approved and live, covering risk, security, cost, data and legal considerations, and taking the change through the bank’s governance and approval process

  • Line manage, coach and develop your team, setting a high bar for delivery and for the responsible use of AI

  • Understanding of privacy and safety considerations when applying LLMs in production, and of how to prove and monitor accuracy once a solution is live – ideally in a regulated environment

description:
We are looking for a Data Scientist to join the Business Analytics team within Spotify’s Business Strategy and Insights organization. You will work with the Audiobooks Analytics Lead to help shape our global audiobooks strategy and improve the experience for listeners, creators, publishers, and authors.

In this role, you will use data analysis, experimentation, and statistical modeling to evaluate some of the most important opportunities facing our audiobooks business. Your work will span content and catalog strategy, discovery and recommendations, subscriber growth, and new product and commercial initiatives. You will turn complex questions into clear recommendations and help senior leaders make confident decisions.

You will collaborate with a distributed team of analysts, data scientists, business leaders, product managers, editorial partners, and engineers. At Spotify, you will have access to rich datasets and the autonomy to explore them creatively and rigorously. Above all, your work will help shape how the world listens to and discovers audiobooks.


What You'll Do
  • Develop data-driven strategies for audiobook catalog, content discovery, listener engagement, and subscriber growth.
  • Evaluate new product, content, licensing, and commercial opportunities through forecasting, scenario modeling, and impact measurement.
  • Partner with Editorial, Personalization, Product, Finance, and Business teams to improve title selection, recommendation quality, and the listener experience.
  • Design and analyze experiments, including A/B tests and quasi-experiments, to measure the impact of product and go-to-market initiatives.
  • Monitor the health of the audiobooks business, identify emerging opportunities or risks, and translate them into clear recommendations.
  • Develop reliable analytical datasets, tools, and reporting that make important insights accessible and repeatable.
  • Work with analytics engineering and data partners to improve data quality and create scalable ways of working.
  • Present findings and recommendations to senior leaders, influencing the direction of our product and business.

    • Who You Are
  • You have 3+ years of professional experience in data science or analytics, ideally in consumer technology, media, subscriptions, marketplaces, or a similarly complex business.
  • You are fluent in SQL and proficient in Python, R, or another programming language, with a strong grasp of statistical methods, experimentation, and causal inference.
  • You combine analytical rigor with strong business judgment and can cleanly extract the “so what” from complex analysis.
  • You are comfortable working through ambiguous problems, structuring open-ended questions, and identifying a practical path forward.
  • You enjoy collaborating with a wide range of cross-functional partners and can build trust across technical and non-technical teams.
  • You are an excellent communicator who can present complex findings clearly to senior leaders and audiences with different levels of technical knowledge.
  • You have a degree in Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience with product analytics, recommendation systems, content businesses, or digital marketplaces is a plus.

    • Where You'll Be
  • This role is based in London.
  • We offer flexibility to work where you work best. There will be some in-person meetings, while still allowing flexibility to work from home.
    • Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

What we're looking for

This is the first dedicated Product Operations hire at Omnea. You'll report to our VP Product.

You'll live at the intersection of product and AI. You'll build the operational layer a fast-growing product team needs: the tool stack, the launch rhythm, our top-level metrics, early access programmes, the comms.

Treat the product org as your user. Define the problem, build the thing, get people using it, then check whether it made anyone faster. If it didn't, kill it and try something else.

We want a structured operator with low ego and a builder's instinct. You'd rather automate a problem than write a process doc about it. You'll be hands-on — wiring up integrations, writing Claude skills, pulling data, shipping dashboards.

What Can You Expect?

AI enablement for the product team. You'll work out where PMs, designers and engineers are spending time they shouldn't, then build the agents, Claude skills and automations that take it off them: synthesising customer signal from Gong, Slack and support, turning specs into first drafts, generating release notes, assembling reporting. Getting people to use what you build matters as much as building it, so expect to spend real time on adoption and coaching. Hold yourself to whether the team is measurably faster.

The product tool stack. Claude (incl skills), Figma, Linear, Notion, Pylon, Mixpanel, Datadog, Granola, our AI tooling, whatever comes next. You own how it's configured, how it connects and how well it's used. Kill what isn't earning its licence. Run the evaluation when we need something new. Connect them up so nobody's copy-pasting between systems. And structure our sources of truth — roadmap data, decision logs, product knowledge — so agents can read them as well as people can.

Launch and release coordination. The product launch calendar, readiness criteria, and a reliable record of what shipped when. The important part is the join between what we build and how we sell it. Product Marketing owns the narrative and the campaign and marketing release timing; you own the reality underneath it. You’ll know the product inside & out, you’ll ensure that the thing we're announcing has actually shipped, works, is documented for internal teams and customer, and a customer can use it on day one. Nothing goes out before it's ready. Nothing meaningful ships without the market hearing about it.

Early access programmes. Alpha, beta and design partner programmes are how we de-risk what we build and how our best customers get a stake in the roadmap. They run informally today. As we sell to bigger and more demanding enterprises they need proper structure: who gets in, what both sides commit to, how feedback gets captured and routed, and what has to be true before something goes GA. You'll design that and mature it as our customer base does.

Top-level metrics. PMs own the detail for their own areas and should keep owning it. You own the layer above: our North Star and company-level product metrics, the key metric from each team pulled into one picture, kept current and actually looked at. You’ll shape the narrative around the metrics and work with PMs to connect the detail into the company level. You'll bring in the signals from outside product that should be shaping decisions — pipeline and what we're winning on, customer health, how people really use what we've shipped. Board and investor materials should pull from your view rather than getting rebuilt from scratch every quarter.

Product comms, including the roadmap deck. The internal newsletter, release notifications, release tracking. As we ship faster this becomes the difference between a business that's aligned and one that's guessing — Sales, Customer and Marketing should never be surprised by something we've shipped. You'll also own our external-facing roadmap deck, used with prospects and customers and as an internal alignment tool.

Documentation. Integration guides, technical docs and product reference material that get used live in sales cycles and onboarding. You'll keep them accurate as the product grows, you’ll track their adoption and adjust.

How the product team comes together. A team growing this fast needs coherence. You'll run our quarterly or semi-annual product events, and wider R&D events where it makes sense, with a real agenda and a real outcome rather than a day of slides. You'll also own our learning rhythm: lunch and learns, internal teach-ins, and getting good external speakers in from other product orgs.

About You

  • You've spent 2 to 3 years in product operations, product management, business operations, strategy and ops, consulting or a chief-of-staff role, ideally in B2B SaaS. The strongest candidates will have done more than one of those, and will have built the systems they ran rather than inherited them.

  • AI is already how you work. Not something you're planning to get to. You use it instinctively, and more usefully, you know how to design systems that leverage it for other people. You've built agents, automations or internal tools that others adopted and kept using. You can get to a working prototype without waiting for engineering.

  • You're comfortable with data. You can pull it, interrogate it and turn it into something a PM will act on.

  • You're a systems thinker. You know the difference between a process problem and a structural one, and when to optimise versus when to redesign.

  • You write well. You can take a roadmap, a release, or a pile of signals from across the business and make it land with people who didn't build it.

  • You can hold an event with a lot of moving parts and senior people in it, and land it.

  • You have experience in a start up or scale-up environment.

title: Performance Marketing Lead
description:
Our Mission

At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: procurement – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger 50+ emails, and pull in Finance, Legal, Security, and IT just to get something approved.

We’ve raised $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, and Accel to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.

The opportunity is massive. Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the 4th fastest growing startup in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.

Our team previously scaled Tessian (cybersecurity tech, backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel, acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The role

We're hiring the first dedicated owner of Omnea's performance marketing.

You're not starting from scratch. Paid campaigns, the website and our social channels all exist (and are working to varying degrees). But nobody's job is to work out what actually produces pipeline and then make more of it. That's this role: take what's already running, find the ROI, and professionalise it into something we can be proud of.

In one week you might work out why a paid campaign is generating leads that never convert, rebuild the landing page that's losing them, build a new LinkedIn audience off the back of our closed-won data, and show the exec team what the pipeline picture looks like.

If you want to run one channel and hand-off the numbers, this might not be for you. If you want to own the loop from spend through to pipeline, and have the data to prove what worked, it is.

You'll work closely with our digital agency partners, the field marketers running events in the UK and US, and the sales team who rely on the pipeline you generate.

What you'll own

Pipeline and performance

You'll build the picture of what marketing is actually returning, and you'll be the person with the answer when someone asks whether a channel is worth the money.

  • Own the pipeline number for our digital channels: how much, from where, and at what cost

  • Build and maintain dashboards in Dreamdata using sources like HubSpot and GA4

  • Track campaigns from first touch through to closed won, and use what you find to change what we run next

  • Run a proper testing cadence. Set the test, call the result, and stop the things that aren't working

  • Report on what the numbers mean, not only what they are

Paid

You own paid. Our agency handles campaign build and optimisation, and you set the direction they work to.

  • Act as day-to-day partner to the agency: set the brief, shape audience strategy and funnel design, and decide together what to test next and how to deploy 6-figure annual ad spend.

  • Own LinkedIn as our primary paid channel: audiences, target account lists, retargeting and sequencing

  • Build audiences from our own data: closed-won patterns, target accounts, product signals - rather than off-the-shelf targeting

  • Work with content and design teammates to produce compelling content

  • Make the case for more budget when the numbers justify it

Website and conversion

  • Own conversion across the site: forms, journeys, page structure, and what happens after someone clicks an ad

  • Build and update pages using our existing component library and CMS

  • Run an ongoing testing programme on the pages that matter, and work with the in-house design team on what comes next

  • Ship landing pages for campaigns and product launches, including forms and tracking

  • Keep tracking and attribution clean, so the reporting can be trusted

What we're looking for

  • Experience in a B2B marketing role, in-house or agency. We care more about what you delivered than where you did it.

  • You're commercial. You think in pipeline and cost per opportunity, not clicks and impressions, and you can tell the difference between a campaign that's busy and one that's working.

  • You know paid mechanics properly. Audiences, match rates, attribution windows, frequency. LinkedIn Ads specifically.

  • You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a report from scratch, spot when something looks wrong, and explain a trend to someone who wasn't in the weeds with you.

  • You've built pages in a CMS. Not from scratch in code — assembling pages from components, keeping them consistent, and getting the tracking right.

  • You've worked with or inside an agency, so you know how to write a brief and how to tell good work from work that's merely on time.

Nice to have

  • Comfortable in tools like HubSpot, Dreamdata, Google Ads, Campaign Manager

  • B2B SaaS, ideally selling to finance, procurement, legal or risk

  • SEO fundamentals

  • Enough Figma to work sensibly with designers

What good looks like in six months

  • We know what every pound of adspend returns, and everyone trusts the number

  • Paid is producing pipeline we can attribute, at a cost we're happy to scale

  • Our LinkedIn audiences are built from our own data rather than off-the-shelf targeting

  • The pages that carry the most traffic have been tested and improved

  • You're the person the exec team asks when they want to know whether a channel is working

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

A few things to note:

  • We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here.

  • We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here

  • We're commercial, ambitious and we don't pretend otherwise! We're actively seeking folks looking to make the most of a career-defining opportunity, with the hunger to be part of building something really impressive. You can see our values here and our Omnea Future Founder's fund here!

  • We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background).

We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow!

title: Senior Customer Support Engineer
description:
About Fyxer

Since launching in May 2024 we've grown to $30 million in ARR. Fyxer is building an AI executive assistant that handles emails, scheduling and follow-up, freeing people in client-facing roles to focus on their customers.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the hardest technical tickets in the business end to end, including the customer conversation, from first report through to resolution

  • Dogfood Fyxer’s own products, give feedback, and influence our roadmap

  • Establish blast radius before escalating, because one customer reporting something is a ticket and forty-seven accounts in the same broken state is an incident

  • Call bug, incident or user error correctly and quickly, and declare it when it's an incident

  • Write escalations Engineering can act on without a single follow-up question, and stay on them until they land

  • Spot patterns across Linear and the queue, raising a tracker before the fifth report of something becomes the tenth

  • Reduce the need for your own role through runbooks, saved queries, Parahelp knowledge, and hands-on upskilling of our senior agents

Here's the honest version of why this role exists. In one recent three-month window we escalated 47 tickets to Engineering and two of them were resolved. Engineering is capacity-constrained, and a third of what we sent them was correctly deprioritised. So this isn't a role that escalates better, it's one that resolves. You'll be backed by strong Customer Success and Product Engineering teams, and given read-only access to our codebase through Cursor, to our data through our internal tooling, and to our production logs to do it.

What Success Looks Like

  • You resolve a growing share of technical escalations without Engineering ever being involved

  • Your escalations are complete, so Engineer can act on them quickly

  • You use AI and you catch it when it's wrong, before it reaches a customer

  • You hold a customer's confidence while you investigate, rather than handing them back to someone else

  • Our senior agents are visibly more capable six months in than they are today, because of you

  • You're the person the team wants on the ticket because they trust your judgement.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years in a technical support role within a SaaS or cloud-based company

  • API fluency: you can read an API reference, reason about authentication, and say what a 401 rather than a 500 tells you about where the fault sits

  • SQL you write yourself: given an unfamiliar schema you work out how the tables relate and write the join unaided

  • Comfortable in logs, following a request across services and working backwards from an error

  • Strong written communication, particularly to a customer who is unhappy

  • Experience with customer support tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, Jira, Linear, others

  • Startup-ready: adaptable, fast-moving, and hands-on

We're not asking for production engineering experience or a computer science degree. We care what you can do, not how you got there.

Location and other bits

  • Based in our Chancery Lane office in London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays from home

  • Standard office hours

  • Benefits include: on-site gym, private medical, pension and lunch provided everyday

The Hiring Process

  1. Submit your CV (no need for a cover letter)

  2. We'll review it

  3. An initial call with someone from the hiring team to review your experience and motivation for joining (30 mins)

  4. A call with our Head of Customer Support on your experience and how you think technically (30 minutes)

  5. A live technical exercise (60 minutes)

  6. Meet more of the team (30 minutes)

For the exercise we'll give you access to a small example application, a database, an API and its logs, a couple of days ahead, along with three customer tickets. You don't need to solve anything in advance, and you're welcome to use whatever AI tooling you normally would, because that's how the job actually works. We'll be paying attention to how you check its answers.

Our Culture

Our culture is intentional. It stems from the fact we're in the race of our lives to reshape one of the largest AI opportunities that exist; email. There is only first or last.

We're going to win by:

  • An obsession around the fact that every second counts, we have to move fast with intensity and drive hard every day.

  • Never let it slide, be relentless in challenging yourself and others to strive for the best outcome.

This culture is intense; it requires focus and discipline. So we'll do everything we can to remove distraction, support your wellbeing, and reward your impact

 

Compensation: £65K – £75K • £65K – £75K Equity

title: Safeguarding Officer
company: Norwich City College of Further and Higher Education
description:
Safeguarding Officer

30 hours per week, 38 weeks per year

APTC Scale SO1, £21,025 to £22,408 actual per annum

Please note that this role is based at Norwich but there is weekly travel required to our Paston site.

Safeguarding Officer

Are you a passionate safeguarding professional committed to making a positive difference in the lives of young people?

We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated individual to join our Wellbeing team and play a key role in promoting the safety, wellbeing and success of our students.

The successful candidate will bring substantial experience in safeguarding and child protection, ideally gained within a social work, education or related setting. You will work collaboratively as part of a multi-disciplinary Wellbeing team, providing support to students and, where appropriate, making referrals to Children's and Adult Social Care and other specialist services.

This is an exciting opportunity for an exceptional communicator who thrives in partnership working. You will build strong relationships with colleagues, students and external agencies, taking a lead role in multi-agency working to ensure the best possible outcomes for young people.

The role requires excellent organisational and administrative skills, with the ability to manage a busy and varied caseload, maintain accurate records and coordinate support effectively. A keen eye for detail, sound professional judgement and the ability to prioritise competing demands are essential.

In return, you will join a supportive and dedicated team, working in a rewarding environment where your expertise will have a direct impact on students' lives.

Key requirements:

  • Extensive experience in safeguarding and child protection.
  • A relevant professional qualification.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience of working effectively with multi-agency partners.
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Confidence in managing sensitive information and maintaining accurate records.
  • A commitment to improving outcomes for children, young people and vulnerable adults.

Please note that some occasional evening work (for example a case where a referral has been in progress during the day and runs on after 5pm) will be required as part of this role.

For an informal conversation about the role or to ask any questions, please contact Helen Richardson-Hulme, Vice Principal Inclusion Safeguarding and Student Services. Please email helen.richardson-hulme@ccn.ac.uk in the first instance. We welcome conversations with prospective candidates interested in working in Student Services.

title: Signer/Communicator
description:
Term Time | Permanent | £14,912 Per Annum (Pro Rata of £30,236 Per Annum)


Who we are

Winner of the Best Place to Work at the Tech South West Awards 2025, City College Plymouth offers a culture the College is proud of. Our core values of Respect, Ownership and Integrity help create an environment that supports a passion for teaching and learning. These values guide our work as we enrich our community through knowledge, experience and skills so every student can achieve their best.

As one of the country’s largest providers of quality education and training, City College Plymouth is entering a period of transition to enable us to propel education into the future. We take pride in offering a learning environment and organisational culture that contribute positively to the health, wellbeing and sustainability of our community and enable all our students and staff to achieve their full potential.


The Role

The main purpose of this post is to provide a graduated and person-centred approach to supporting students with a Hearing Impairment and/or Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) within a post-16 learning environment.

You will support students to access the curriculum, participate fully in learning and college life, experience achievement, and develop greater confidence and independence in their learning and wider life skills.

A key aspect of the role will be supporting students with a Hearing Impairment through effective communication, including the use of British Sign Language (BSL). The successful candidate may also be required to provide BSL communication/signing support for individual students on a 1:1 basis, depending on their identified needs and the provision required to enable them to access their programme of study.

You will have knowledge and experience of supporting students with Hearing Impairment and SEND, alongside a genuine commitment to making a positive difference to students' educational experiences. You will work collaboratively with teaching staff, Learning Support colleagues and other professionals to promote inclusion, independence and high expectations for all students.

Above all, you will be committed to ensuring that our students receive an inclusive, supportive and outstanding educational experience.


What Will You Bring to the Role

  • Adapting: You will need to adapt your communication and support approach to meet the individual needs of students with Hearing Impairment and/or SEND.
  • Collaborating: You will work closely with students, teaching staff, Learning Support colleagues and other professionals.
  • Focused & Attentive: You will need to remain focused and attentive to students' individual needs while supporting them within busy post-16 learning environments.
  • Persistence: You will demonstrate patience, persistence and determination when supporting students to overcome barriers to learning, communication and participation.

description:
About Drumbeat School

Drumbeat School is a sector leading specialist provision for children and young people aged 4–19 with Autism. We are committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment where every pupil can thrive.

About the Role

We are looking for a friendly, caring and proactive Lunchtime Supervisor to join our school community.

Lunchtime is such an important part of the day with rich learning opportunities for our pupils.

You will be part of a supportive team that looks after pupils in the dining hall and playground encouraging independence and supporting social and emotional aspects of pupils needs.

From helping younger children with their lunch to leading playtime activities, you’ll bring warmth, patience and energy to every day.

This role is perfect for someone who enjoys working with children and wants to make a real difference in their day.

If you’re reliable, nurturing and have a great sense of fun — we’d love to hear from you

Key Responsibilities

• Encourage appropriate exercise and activities to promote health and well-being
• Supervising pupils during lunch and play, making sure everyone feels safe, included and respected.
• Helping to keep the dining hall and surrounding areas clean, tidy and hygienic
• Supporting children who may need a bit of extra help or encouragement.

• Report any safeguarding concerns in line with the school’s child protection policy
• Building positive relationships with pupils and staff to create a caring lunchtime environment.
• Being a role model for positive behaviour and teamwork

description:

Hours: Full time 37 hours per week, all year round.

Actual Salary: £41,177.45-£45,529.48

Contract: Maternity Cover, Fixed Term for the maximum of 12 months.

Start: October 2026

About the role:


The White Horse Federation is a Multi-Academy Trust of 30 schools in Swindon, Wiltshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire, committed to providing the very best education for our students.

Our Recruitment Team is a key part of the Central Professional Services function, delivering a high-quality and strategic recruitment service across our network of 41 schools and Central Office teams. We are currently recruiting for a Recruitment Lead to join our team on a fixed term basis. This is an on-site role predominantly based at our Central Office in Swindon, where you will lead and develop a team of Recruitment Officers.

The Recruitment Lead will be responsible for overseeing end-to-end recruitment activity across all schools and Central Office functions, ensuring a consistent, efficient and candidate-focused approach to talent acquisition. The role will provide leadership and support to the Recruitment Officers, manage recruitment processes and campaigns, monitor recruitment performance, and drive continuous improvement in attraction and hiring practices. This position would be ideal for an experienced recruitment professional with strong team leadership skills, a proactive approach to stakeholder management, and experience of managing high-volume recruitment within a complex, multi-site organisation.

You will be:

  • Lead and manage the Recruitment Officers, providing day-to-day guidance, support, coaching and performance management to ensure a high-quality recruitment service.
  • Oversee end-to-end recruitment activity across all schools and Central Office functions, ensuring vacancies are filled efficiently and in line with safer recruitment requirements.
  • Manage and continuously improve the Applicant Tracking System (ATS), ensuring recruitment data is accurate, compliant and up to date.
  • Monitor recruitment metrics and performance, producing regular reports and insights for Senior Leaders to support workforce planning and recruitment strategies.
  • Develop and implement attraction strategies to increase candidate quality, diversity and application volumes across a wide range of roles.
  • Build strong relationships with Headteachers, School Leaders and hiring managers, providing expert recruitment advice and guidance throughout the recruitment process.
  • Oversee all advertising activity, ensuring vacancies are effectively promoted through appropriate job boards, social media channels and recruitment campaigns.
  • Ensure compliance with statutory guidance, employment legislation, safeguarding requirements and safer recruitment practices.
  • Manage recruitment administration processes, including offer documentation, onboarding and pre-employment checks, ensuring an excellent candidate experience.
  • Lead recruitment projects and initiatives aimed at improving recruitment efficiency, candidate engagement and employer branding.
  • Work closely with HR and Operations colleagues to support organisational workforce planning and staffing requirements.
  • Manage recruitment-related inboxes and enquiries, ensuring prompt and professional responses to schools, candidates and stakeholders.
  • Support and develop Recruitment Officers through training, mentoring and regular performance reviews.
  • Ensure recruitment records and documentation are maintained accurately and in accordance with GDPR and data protection requirements.
  • Identify trends, risks and opportunities in recruitment activity and make recommendations to improve attraction, retention and recruitment outcomes across the Trust.

We can offer you:

  • A busy and varied role where no two days are the same!
  • A friendly, supportive team who are committed to providing a high-quality service.
  • The opportunity to join a forward-thinking Trust with high aspirations for students, staff and school improvement.
  • Exciting and relevant CPD and career development opportunities.
  • A range of employee benefits including Local Government Pension Scheme, Cycle to Work scheme and employee assistance programme.
  • We are looking for a candidate who:
  • Has organisational skills and an ability to multi-task successfully.
  • Competent in Microsoft Office, Outlook and Teams.
  • Can communicate effectively.


The Advantages of joining our Federation

In addition, our employees reap the rewards of a competitive benefits package, including:

Employee Assistance programme

Ready to apply?

title: Learning Coach
description:
Learning Coaches

Do you love working with children and thrive off seeing them become independent brilliant learners? Then, this is a wonderful opportunity to make a difference.

You don’t have to be necessarily academic to work here. We do want people who are resilient, care about children, passionate about education, want to make a difference and who have the humour to find ways through every day.

The post is a fixed term post until 31st December 2026 with potential for extension, term time only plus one week (39 weeks per year)

Full and Part Time roles available

SCP 5-6 £25,989 - £26,403 FTE depending on experience

EYFS, KS 1 or KS 2

We are recruiting:

Our Learning Coaches are people who:

  • understand children.

  • are kind, thoughtful and courageous.

  • step outside of their comfort zones.

  • willing to learn, and,

  • able to build supportive relationships with adults and children in our community.

Everyone is welcome and everyone is included. If you can demonstrate a thirst for learning and an ability to rise above challenges (and importantly to celebrate successes together) then this is the place for you. We are looking for team members who celebrate our inclusive school and enjoy working with learners with a diverse range of needs.

The University of Cambridge Primary School aspires to be an outstanding school and as well as this responsibility, we will work closely with partners, including the Faculty of Education and the wider University, to develop initial teacher training and research. The school is the first primary University Training School - expectations are very high.

Our Learning Coaches have a big role in our school, and many are inspired to take on some leadership of an area (e.g. first aid, Speech & Language, STEM), being fully involved in managing a wonderful lunch experience for children and need to be flexible. We work differently at UCPS to develop and encourage a community of educators who collaborate to support each child during their unique learning journey. Being a part of the first university training school in the country is very exciting.

   Our school can offer you:

  • An opportunity for you to make a real difference in the lives of our young people

  • A supportive leadership team to help you thrive

  • A welcoming and enthusiastic environment with a talented and dedicated staff team

  • Lots of singing and community spirit!

The successful candidate will need to:

  • Be kind and have courage.

  • Be able to adapt the role to a changing educational landscape and to support staff through this.

  • Be willing to step out of your comfort zone to find ways through and be solution focused.

  • Be hard working.

  • Have high personal expectations and dedication to achieve the best with the children you teach and support.

  • Be willing to undertake the appropriate training to support children with intimate care.

  • Interest and positive attitude to support class teachers in delivering planned activities as well as in managing groups of children. 

  • You have good Literacy and Numeracy skills, able to support children in reading, writing and maths.

  • Talk about education and our values, giving examples how they live these in their own lives and contexts

  • Ability to work collaboratively with all members of the community.

All staff are employed by the UTS Cambridge Trust not the University of Cambridge.

(Same contract as with Teaching Assistants)

Closing Date: 8th September 2026

Shortlisting: 9th September 2026

Interview date: Monday 14th September 2026

For further information and to make an application please visit www.universityprimaryschool.org.uk Please note that CVs are not accepted.

title: Sales Completion Specialist
description:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

We're after someone to join our Sales Completion team - the beating heart of our business. Our platform is changing the game for car sellers and dealers, making it easier and fairer for everyone. But a bit of tech can only go so far; that's where you come in. You'll be the expert guide for our customers, helping them get the best price for their car. It's a bit like being a brilliant matchmaker, but instead of people, it's cars and cash. You’ll be right in the middle of it all, negotiating, problem-solving, and celebrating with customers. We're a team that loves to learn, so you'll have loads of opportunities to grow your skills, take on new challenges, and really make your mark.

What you'll do

  • Be the trusted expert for car sellers, delivering a seamless, can-do post-auction experience.

description:

Job Description

Are you an experienced construction project leader with the commercial acumen to deliver complex infrastructure projects while managing the expectations of lenders, investors and key stakeholders?

We are looking for an experienced Senior Construction Project Manager to fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role across Elgin’s utility-scale solar PV, BESS and co-located PV/BESS projects. The role is focused on leading multidisciplinary project teams within a single Elgin delivery framework, ensuring that finance, legal, engineering, procurement, construction, operations, route-to-market and external adviser inputs are coordinated into one clear project position from late stage development / FID through construction, commissioning, commercial operations and handover to Asset Management. Particular emphasis will be placed on lender, investor, SPV governance and internal delivery interfaces.
 
This role requires significant project and contract management experience, including direct involvement in project finance processes, lender due diligence, conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender reporting, waivers / consents and coordination with lender technical advisers. The successful candidate will need specific experience with FIDIC based Construction Contracts, strong commercial judgement, disciplined contract administration capability and the ability to translate project delivery status into clear funding, governance and decision-making outputs.
 
To be successful in the role, you will have experience representing a client, employer, sponsor or SPV in the delivery of complex infrastructure or renewable energy projects. You will be commercially astute, highly organised, confident leading multidisciplinary project teams through a common governance and delivery framework, and capable of engaging credibly with lenders, investors, advisers, contractors, shareholder forums and senior internal stakeholders.

What you will be do:

  • Fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role for allocated projects, ensuring Elgin’s SPV, governance, commercial and contractual obligations are actively managed from FID through COD and handover.
  • Lead project and contract management on project-financed assets, coordinating lender processes including conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender technical adviser queries, lender reporting, waivers / consents and funding milestone submissions.
  • Administer and manage high-value EPC, ICP and related project contracts, including notices, variations, claims, payment applications, completion milestones, liquidated damages, defects and close-out obligations.
  • Maintain disciplined project controls across programme, budget, cash flow, risk, actions, decisions and change, ensuring transparent reporting to senior management, SPV governance bodies, lenders and investors.
  • Act as the primary project coordination point between Elgin’s internal project team, finance, legal, procurement, engineering, construction, operations, route-to-market and external advisers, ensuring that all workstreams operate from one integrated delivery plan, one risk position and one set of decision requirements.
  • Lead and manage multidisciplinary internal project teams within Elgin’s agreed delivery framework by setting priorities, clarifying accountabilities, managing dependencies, aligning workstreams to project milestones and escalating decisions in a timely and structured manner.
  • Manage the relationship and reporting cadence with project finance lenders, equity investors, shareholder representatives, lender technical advisers and other key finance-facing stakeholders, including preparing and presenting clear, decision-ready updates for shareholder forums and related governance meetings.
  • Oversee contractor, owner’s engineer and technical adviser interfaces to ensure delivery evidence, technical outputs and contractual positions support Elgin’s funding, governance and employer obligations.
  • Proactively identify commercial, contractual, programme and financing risks, develop mitigation plans and ensure issues are escalated with clear options, recommendations and decision requirements.
  • Support tendering, contract negotiation and commercial strategy by ensuring delivery arrangements are bankable, financeable, contractually robust and aligned with lender / investor expectations.


Your profile

What you will need: 

  • Degree in project management, construction management, engineering, or similar.
  • Extensive experience in infrastructure, renewables, power, energy storage or comparable capital projects, with significant project and contract management responsibility.
  • Direct experience working on project-financed projects, including lender due diligence, , funding drawdowns, lender technical adviser processes and ongoing lender / investor reporting.
  • Strong understanding of the Client / Employer’s Representative role and experience representing an owner, SPV, sponsor or employer in the delivery of complex contracted projects.
  • Extensive experience administering FIDIC, EPC, ICP and construction management contracts, including notices, variations, claims, payment mechanisms, completion tests, liquidated damages and contractual close-out.
  • Demonstrable ability to lead multidisciplinary internal teams and align finance, legal, engineering, procurement, construction, operations and external adviser inputs around delivery milestones within a standardised delivery framework.
  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to assess risk versus reward, protect the employer’s position and communicate implications clearly to senior stakeholders.
  • Experience preparing and presenting concise, decision-ready reports for senior management, investment committees, SPV boards, lenders, investors, shareholder forums and other governance forums, with the ability to translate complex programme, commercial, technical and financing issues into clear options and recommendations.
  • Working knowledge of utility-scale solar PV, BESS, grid connection and route-to-market interfaces, with sufficient technical understanding to challenge contractors and advisers effectively.
  • Highly organised and proficient in Microsoft Office and project controls tools, with strong written communication, meeting management and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Valid driver’s license for Ireland and the UK.

At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.

Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 700 experts from 35+ countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.


Your future position

Join Kpler’s Chartering team as a Junior Market Data Analyst – Chartering and play a key role in ensuring the quality and accuracy of the data that powers our Chartering products.

Kpler’s Chartering products rely on accurate vessel, ownership and market data to help charterers, shipowners and brokers make informed commercial decisions. In this role, you will work hands-on with the datasets behind these products, investigating inconsistencies, validating information and helping improve data quality at scale.

Your work will span a range of chartering datasets, from vessel ownership and characteristics to fixtures, cargo orders, vessel positions and shipping zones. You will use SQL and Python to extract, transform and analyse data, build validation checks and investigate potential issues. 

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting into the detail of data, asking why something doesn't look right and finding ways to identify and solve problems systematically. You will work closely with Product, Data, Research, Engineering and AI/ML teams, turning individual data issues into broader improvements across Kpler's datasets and products.

  • Monitor, validate and improve the quality of key datasets supporting Kpler's Chartering products.
  • Investigate data gaps, inconsistencies and customer-reported issues, using data analysis to understand their root causes and drive them through to resolution.
  • Curate and validate vessel ownership, commercial management, operator information and relevant vessel characteristics.
  • Review and benchmark AI-parsed fixtures, identifying recurring extraction errors and building validation approaches to measure and improve parsing quality.
  • Use SQL to query large datasets, including cargo and AIS data, to investigate potential issues and identify incorrect or inconsistent information at scale.
  • Use Python notebooks to extract, transform and analyse data and develop validation scripts and repeatable quality checks.
  • Maintain and improve Kpler's chartering-specific shipping zones and geographical mappings, using tools such as QGIS.
  • Work with Product, Data, Research, Engineering and AI/ML teams to provide structured feedback and help improve the quality of underlying datasets and extraction processes.
  • Translate individual data-quality issues into systematic improvements where appropriate, identifying patterns rather than only correcting individual records.
  • Contribute to the development of new analytical views and algorithms as the Chartering product evolves, including areas such as CPP/DPP and projected vessels.
  • Help establish and track data-quality metrics, benchmarks and processes as Chartering datasets expand.

  • 1–3 years of experience in data analysis, market research, maritime/shipping, commodities or a related analytical role.

  • Proven hands-on experience with Python, including working in notebooks and using Python for data analysis, transformation or validation.
  • Strong Excel / Google Sheets skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with excellent attention to detail and an ability to identify patterns and inconsistencies in data.

title: Senior Account Manager
description:
Our market leading power purchase agreement (PPA) platform has been changing how renewable energy is sold in the UK for 10 years and we’re just as ambitious now as we were in 2016. Our locally led segment covers everything from a single small asset through to small portfolios and community energy schemes, with account values typically between £350 and £100,000.

This role has two halves. The first is delighting our biggest clients in our locally led segment. Ensuring they are able to utilise the platform to it's fullest extent and we are understand how we can best support them.

The second is supporting the Head of Client Success on commercial operations across the renewals cycle and taking full ownership of licence exempt supply, Making it worth more to the generator, making it worth more to us, and building the operational machinery that lets it scale beyond a handful of deals. The second is

You will also lead a small team of two: an Account Manager focused on retaining and growing our existing locally led clients, and a Junior Sales Executive focused on winning new ones.

Tasks

Delivering for clients

  • Own a portfolio of key accounts end to end, including running tenders. This is a hands-on role and the majority of the week is spent delivering for your own clients.
  • Manage those accounts strategically: deepen existing relationships, build new ones across the client organisation, and make sure no account depends on a single contact.
  • Identify and convert growth opportunities within accounts, both in client value delivered and in revenue retained and won.
  • Act as the escalation point for the team's accounts and set the standard for how account management is done here, through call coaching, account reviews and shared best practice.

Licence exempt supply, commercial

  • Own the LES proposition end to end for locally led generators: what we offer, to whom, at what price, and why a generator should choose it.
  • Build and maintain the value case. Generators need to compare an LES route alongside a standard utility PPA on a like for like basis, with honest assumptions and objective insights.
  • Work with offtakers and supply partners on LES products and commercial terms, including matching, fees and value distribution.
  • Own the margin. Price so that value is shared fairly between the generator and Renewable Exchange, and so the economics still work at volume.
  • Track the regulatory, levy and market developments that move the value of exempt supply, and translate them into a commercial position the team can actually use.
  • Escalate contractual and regulatory questions to the right internal owner rather than improvising.

Licence exempt supply, operations and systems

  • Design the operating process: eligibility screening, onboarding, data flows, settlement and reconciliation, invoicing, reporting.
  • Build it into our systems, working with the platform, product and finance teams. Manual workarounds are a starting point, not a destination.
  • Write the playbooks, templates and checklists so the process is people agnostic.
  • Report on LES volume, revenue and pipeline to the Head of Client Success and to the wider leadership team.

Commercial operations across the renewals cycle

  • Support the Head of Client Success on renewals forecasting, tender scheduling and pipeline hygiene across the client base.
  • Own the reporting that tells us how the renewals cycle is actually performing, not how we hoped it would.
  • Find and fix the friction. Where the renewals process leaks time, value or clients, propose the change and then deliver it.

Leading the team

  • Line manage two people: an Account Manager and a Junior Sales Executive. One to ones, objectives, development and performance for both.

  • Central Bristol office with bike storage and shower facilities.

title: Senior Talent Partner
description:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the role

Join Faculty as a Senior Talent Partner to lead end-to-end hiring across our high-growth organisation. You will own the recruitment lifecycle for both individual contributor and leadership positions across Applied AI within the commercial space and across our Central Functions.

Beyond filling roles, you will spearhead high-impact projects in employer branding, candidate experience and DE&I. This is a pivotal role for an ambitious professional ready to shape our talent strategy, engage elite passive candidates and ensure Faculty remains the employer of choice in the AI and technology market.

What you'll be doing:

  • Proactively sourcing high-caliber, diverse candidates using innovative techniques and tools to maximise direct hires and build robust talent pipelines.

  • Advising and coaching hiring managers on recruitment best practices, inclusive hiring techniques, and data-driven decision-making.

  • Working on strategic projects related to employer branding, early careers, and candidate experience to amplify Faculty’s presence in the market.

  • Managing the end-to-end recruitment journey, ensuring a fair and inclusive process that prioritises an exceptional experience for every applicant.

  • Collaborating across the business to understand evolving strategy and culture, acting as a brand ambassador at industry meet-ups and conferences.

  • Utilising market insights and data to continuously optimise hiring workflows, identifying trends, and recommending innovative solutions to recruitment challenges.

Who we're looking for:

  • You bring significant experience in end-to-end recruitment from within the commercial and/or central functions space, ideally from within a fast-paced, high-growth technology environment.

  • You possess expert sourcing skills, with a proven ability to identify and engage passive, qualified talent using a broad range of modern tools and methodologies.

  • You are a skilled communicator who can adapt your style to influence senior stakeholders and persuasively articulate Faculty’s mission to candidates.

  • You demonstrate a deep commitment to DE&I, with a track record of successfully integrating inclusive practices into sourcing and selection activities.

  • You thrive on ownership and accountability, using data-driven insights to manage your time effectively and meet ambitious delivery goals.

  • You've demonstrated a clear understanding of how AI is shaping the hiring landscape and changing modern talent strategies.

  • You have a strong grasp of interview evaluation methods and employment compliance, combined with an entrepreneurial mindset that seeks to constantly "raise the bar."

Our Interview Process

  1. Initial Talent Screen (30 mins)

  2. Introductory interview with the Hiring Manager (45 mins)

  3. Competency & Scenario based interview (60 mins)

  4. Final Interview with our Chief People Officer (30 mins)

#LI-PRIO

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

Some of our standout benefits:

  • Unlimited Annual Leave Policy

  • Private healthcare and dental

  • Enhanced parental leave

  • Family-Friendly Flexibility & Flexible working

  • Sanctus Coaching

  • Hybrid Working

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: Senior Operational Finance Manager – 6 Month Fixed Term Contract
description:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Finance Team 👋

At Trainline, our Finance team is the backbone of how we manage, govern, and grow the business responsibly. From transactional processing to financial controls and systems ownership, the team works across a broad range of disciplines to ensure Trainline operates with accuracy, integrity, and commercial rigour. This is a pivotal interim appointment within our operational finance function, sitting within a high-performing team and reporting directly to the Group Financial Controller.

As Interim Senior Operational Finance Manager, you will lead the teams responsible for Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Finance Systems, and our Cashbook function, driving operational excellence and embedding a continuous improvement mindset across the function. You will work closely with Finance leadership and Technology colleagues to strengthen controls, streamline processes, and maintain delivery momentum throughout a six-month fixed-term engagement, with a clear and structured handover at its close.

In this role as the Interim Senior Operational Finance Manager, you will...🚄

  • Lead and develop a multi-disciplinary operational finance team across Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Finance Systems, and Cashbook, setting clear objectives, managing team capacity, and actively supporting the professional growth of every team member.

  • Own the day-to-day management of the AP and AR functions, ensuring invoices, payments, collections, and reconciliations are processed accurately, on time, and in line with strong governance and compliance standards.

  • Drive working capital performance by monitoring AP and AR KPIs, proactively managing aged debt and debtor days, and delivering regular reporting and insight to the Group Financial Controller.

  • Oversee bank and cash reconciliation across all entities and currencies, maintaining robust controls over cash processes including payment authorisation, segregation of duties, and reconciliation review.

  • Act as business owner for Trainline's core finance systems, ensuring platforms are scalable, secure, and well-governed, and that teams are empowered to use them effectively through training and change management.

  • Own the operational finance contribution to month-end close, ensuring ledgers are closed accurately and on time, and serve as a key point of contact throughout internal and external audit processes.

  • Identify and deliver process improvements with a focus on automation, efficiency, and scalability, coordinating with the Senior Finance Manager - Transformation to ensure changes are aligned with the broader Finance transformation roadmap.

  • Build trusted relationships across Finance, Technology, and the wider business, acting as the senior point of contact for operational finance and managing SLAs with internal stakeholders.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Substantial experience managing operational finance functions, ideally spanning Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and finance systems in a fast-paced commercial environment.

  • A strong track record of leading and developing high-performing finance teams, with the ability to set direction, manage performance, and support the professional growth of team members.

  • Solid expertise across AP/AR processes, credit control, working capital management, and financial controls, with a high standard of attention to detail and data governance.

  • Experience working within an ERP environment, ideally Microsoft Dynamics 365 or a comparable platform, with a confident grasp of transactional finance processes end-to-end.

  • A process improvement mindset, with demonstrated success delivering automation and efficiency gains across operational finance functions.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships with stakeholders across Finance, Technology, and senior business leadership.

  • Confidence managing SLAs and service expectations with internal stakeholders, alongside the resilience to operate effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

  • Availability at short notice and comfort operating in an interim capacity, with the drive to take ownership quickly, deliver impact within a defined timeframe, and lead a clear and structured handover.

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

______________________________________________________________________________________________________

title: SEI Instructor Lead
description:
Since 2011, General Assembly (GA) has transformed tens of thousands of careers through pioneering, experiential education in today’s most in-demand skills. As featured in The Economist, Wired, and The New York Times, GA offers training in web development, data, design, marketing, and more, both online and at campuses across multiple countries. Our global professional community boasts more than 95,000 full- and part-time alumni — and counting.

In addition to fostering career growth for individuals, GA helps employers cultivate top diverse tech talent and spur innovation by transforming their teams through strategic learning. More than 21,000 employees at elite companies worldwide have honed their digital fluency with our corporate training programs. GA has also been recognized as one of Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500, and Fast Company has dubbed us leaders in World-Changing Ideas as well as the #1 Most Innovative Company in Education.

Our Software Engineering Immersive course is a life-changing educational experience where our students learn the skills and mindsets to take on new careers as web developers. We are looking for a lead instructor with strong JavaScript experience to play a key role on our growing instructional team. This role is a full-time, temporary position that includes a start and end date for this cohort. There may be potential to receive an additional assignment offering, but additional assignments are not guaranteed.

Why teach our Software Engineering Immersive?

If you are looking to make a life-changing impact by sharing your love for software development with the next generation of developers, we’d love for you to consider joining our team. We deliver more than just skills training, and are looking for teachers who share our vision for a community of lifelong learners pursuing work that they love. As a full-time teacher for our flagship full-time Software Engineering program, you will join us to:

  • Work closely with an instructional team or other support staff to guide students through a rigorous, transformational journey towards a new career in software development.
  • Become a better leader and mentor as you learn from veteran instructors and our world-class instructional coaches.
  • Inspire and support students as they identify their passions and drive their own continued learning beyond the curriculum.
  • Adapt our global curriculum and use it to guide your teaching, building your own lesson plans as needed and sharing your professional lessons learned over time.
  • Facilitate a safe, supportive, and energetic community that welcomes the various needs and learning styles of your students.

What do we teach?

We adapt both our global curriculum and local approach to the technical trends and hiring environment of the times and regions we work in, but today our primary educational approach centers around JavaScript. In general, our curriculum is scaffolded to follow the historical evolution of software engineering. We start by teaching the fundamentals of programming and web design through JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. The course focuses on JavaScript. We cover API development in Node, then tackle one or more front-end MV* frameworks (Backbone, Angular, Ember, React). We also cover all sorts of other things that junior web developers need to know, like source control, team collaboration, and developer workflow.

We give students the chance to spend focused time building at least 4 major projects, in addition to other smaller projects and labs. About 20% of overall class time is spent on dedicated project work.

Skills and Qualifications

  • You are the person that your colleagues naturally gravitate to when they are trying to figure something out.
  • You are eager to shape the skills, minds, and careers of the newest generation of web developers.
  • You have at least 2+ years of experience working on a software development team
  • You are familiar with Computer Science topics, such as: Recursion, Sorting, Search, Linked Lists, Stacks and queues, Sets, Trees, Search Tries, Graphs, Hash tables, and Design patterns
  • You have working experience in both front-end and back-end development, and are fluent in
    • HTML and CSS
    • Full-stack JavaScript (strong JavaScript highly preferred)
    • At least one JS MV* framework (Angular, Backbone, or React preferred)
    • SQL databases (we generally use PosgreSQL)
    • NoSQL (we generally cover MongoDB and Redis)
    • At least one additional object-oriented language (Python preferred
  • Completion of a bachelor’s degree or at least 10 years of applicable experience in lieu of a 4-year degree
  • At least 2 years of practical experience within the last five years; 3 years preferred.
  • Practical experience does not include teaching experience.
  • Good moral character and strong decision making abilities
  • Language, mathematical, reasoning, and computer skills that assure teaching effectiveness.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Teach and facilitate in class instruction Monday-Friday, approximately 8 hours per day, for the 10- 14 week duration of the program.
  • Instructors will need to commit a few hours per week preparing lessons and materials, leveraging existing GA curriculum content.
  • Work closely with co-instructors or teaching assistants to provide students with meaningful and prompt feedback on their progress.
  • Work alongside GA staff and teaching team to best meet the needs and learning styles of your students.
  • Guide students through development of a stellar final project that will showcase their abilities to hiring managers.
  • Facilitate a dynamic, collaborative, and positive classroom community.
  • Inspire students to persevere through the challenges of learning a new skill set

The anticipated compensation range for the full duration of this course in the US market is $23,000 and $27,000. Compensation will be determined based on experience, education, geographic location, and other factors.

US benefit offerings for temporary full-time or part-time employment may include eligibility for dental and vision coverage. Available paid leave may include paid time off and holiday pay.

The salary range published in this job posting is for US based locations only. Non-US based candidates interested in this position can email talent@generalassemb.ly for country specific pay range details and benefits offered.

Licensure:
General Assembly is a regulated provider of higher education, and some states require instructors to be licensed to teach. During the onboarding period, you will be required to be approved as an instructor in relevant states. Directions for becoming licensed will be shared with you during onboarding. Licensure requirements vary by state, but you may be required to provide academic transcripts and to answer questions pertaining to moral character, professional conduct, education, and work history. (CO, TX, GA, WA, DC, Toronto, CA, IL, UT, NY.) General Assembly will pay for all licensing fees.

Unless otherwise noted, remote positions can be performed from the following approved General Assembly operating countries.

United States of America (states of operation may vary), Canada (provinces of operation may vary), United Kingdom, Australia, and Singapore.

  • You’ll bring curiosity, humility and a willingness to learn, while growing your engineering judgement and technical confidence over time

What We’re Looking For

THE STATS

What we’re looking for in our next teammate

  • Some experience building backend software through work, internships, placements, bootcamps, university projects or personal projects
  • An understanding of Java or a similar object-oriented programming language, and an interest in developing backend services and APIs
  • Familiarity with databases and SQL, with an interest in learning more about data modelling, performance and scaling
  • Awareness of common data structures, algorithms and software design principles
